title: Planning to buy a lyricon to ease his embouchure problem
summary: Herman plans to buy a lyricon, through Tom Scott's contacts, because electronics avoid his embouchure problem; reactions to its sound on the album have been good.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: And my -- and adding to that little bonfire, I hope, will start -- I'm now in the throes of making arrangements to buy for my very own a -- now I have to think of the name of the instrument.

Yes. And Tom Scott is checking out with the people in Boston who build them, and the newest model is his grandchild, and I'm very interested in getting one and starting to apply it to the bunsen burner.
I see. So you are seriously going to --

I would like to try and cope with things because of a basic embouchure problem I have. I feel this is a logical move, and if I can come up with something interesting, I feel that it should have definite appeal, if it's used tastefully. It should have definite appeal with some of the young players around the country, and I'd like to be in on it.
Yeah. And then would decrease the problems of the embouchure with the clarinet.
That's right, because when you're dealing with electronics, you don't have an embouchure problem.
Uh-huh. Have there been inquiries about Tom's playing at all, or comments on the album using the Lyricom?
Well, all I know is that the reaction has been that it's weird and it sounds beautiful.
Yeah, that's been the general reaction.
So I'm hoping to pick up the trail somewhere along the line.
Yeah, your alertness through the years of just this kind of thing, looking at what might be a possibility with high potential, I think, has been very consistent.
Well, that's the challenge of trying to come up with something that isn't the run of the mill. And this I'm interested in, generally.
